analysis:
Vistra fell 6.7%, underperforming the market by 2.3 percentage points but holding up better than the median of its AI power and infrastructure peers, which dropped 7.7%. The coverage points to a broader selloff across data center and power infrastructure stocks, with headlines describing plunges in fuel cell companies and noting "forced control on CapEx" pressuring data center plays. One item mentions VST falling 14% on a Texas election vote, while another discusses year-to-date declines of 25%, suggesting ongoing sector weakness beyond today's session.

The company reports earnings tomorrow. Past reactions show a typical move of around 2.1 percentage points beyond what the market alone would explain, with earnings beats not reliably leading to gains—the May 2026 report beat by 53% yet produced a negative abnormal move of 5.3 points. Estimates have edged up slightly over the last 30 days to $2.43, though they're down from $2.59 three months ago, with one revision in each direction recently.
